text:
ravi: Quick heads-up — found a behavior in Private control-plane routing for on-prem tenants with strict egress whitelists. When the smart router chooses a cheaper model variant in a different region, the control plane currently replies with a 200 and a redirect, but the local proxy still tries an egress call and gets blocked.

hana: Ugh. Can you paste the control-plane decision payload you saw?

ravi: Sure, log excerpt:
```json
{
  "tenant": "acme-inc",
  "route_decision": "route_to_variant",
  "variant": "gpt-small-eu",
  "instructions": {
    "endpoint": "https://eu-infer.redwood/api",
    "egress_required": true
  }
}
```

ravi: The problem is egress_required is true, but the tenant has an egress whitelist that doesn't include eu-infer, so the proxy should've converted this into a local-failover decision (or explicit deny) instead of returning a redirect.

liam: That sounds like a gap between policy evaluation and decision serialization. Control plane should include an explicit flag that says "egress_allowed": true/false so proxies don't try and then fail.

maria: @ravi can we show this state in the Console? Need a visible reason why a request was prevented vs why we routed. Customers keep asking if the model choice caused errors.

ravi: Agreed. Minimal change proposal: add decision fields: `egress_allowed` (bool), `egress_reason` (string short code), and `route_confidence` (0-1). That way proxies can short-circuit.

hana: Telemetry note: instrument control_plane.decision.{egress_allowed,egress_reason} and increment a per-tenant counter for blocked_egress_attempts. That gives us a dashboard to show the customer and for oncall.

liam: For API contract I'd propose this snippet for the control-plane response: 
```json
{
  "status": "ok",
  "route_action": "forward|deny|local_failover",
  "egress_allowed": false,
  "egress_reason": "whitelist_mismatch"
}
```
This way proxies only attempt egress if route_action==forward && egress_allowed==true.

maria: UX: add an inline badge on the tenant Routing page that shows "egress blocked" with a tooltip that surfaces egress_reason and a one-click override for org-admins (backend flag that expires after 5 minutes). We need guardrails to prevent accidental escapes from the whitelist.

ravi: We should also treat fallback variants as "costly" penalties in scoring so the router prefers same-region model variants even if slightly more expensive, when egress is not allowed. Otherwise we'll continually propose unreachable routes.

liam: Implementation plan:
- control-plane: policy evaluator returns a decision object with egress_allowed + reason (PR)
- proxy: honor egress_allowed, and map deny -> short-circuit 403 with user-friendly error
- console: expose blocked_egress_attempts and an admin override button (A/B with safety)
- telemetry: add metrics + traces tagging decision_reason

ops-bot: deploy:policy-evaluator v2 promoted to staging by @liam — CI passed. (build 2026-03-18T09:12:10Z) :rocket:

hana: sgtm. @liam can you open a small PR for the response schema and a companion PR in proxy to short-circuit? I can pick up the Console card.

liam: Yup — opened https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4567 with schema & tests. Proxy PR incoming.

maria: Thanks folks. Let's also add a simple e2e that simulates an on-prem agent with a denied egress and assert we return actionable error text (not a redirect).

ravi: Will add the e2e to the plan. Thanks all :thumbsup:
